newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico ports handle record cargo in 1996 -gov't.
newsitem.headline: Mexico ports handle record cargo in 1996 -gov't.

text.p: Mexican ports handled record levels of cargo in 1996, an 11 percent increase over the previous year, the government's port administration authority said in a report obtained by Reuters on Monday.
Total cargo volume rose to 206.7 million tonnes in 1996 from 186.3 million tonnes the year before, the study said.

"If one observes the dynamism registered in recent years, shipping is a sector with a very encouraging investor outlook," Pedro Pablo Zepeda, the head of Ports and Merchant Navy under the Transport and Communications Ministry, said in the report.

Mexico is in the continuing process of privatizing port operations, and most recently sold port operating rights to Ensenada port, on the northwest corner of the Baja California peninsula, to Philippine International Container Terminal Services.
Zepeda credited initial privatization in 1996 with lowering costs and improving operations.
For example, at Manzanillo and Lazaro Cardenas ports on Mexico's Pacific Coast, labor costs per tonne dropped to two pesos in 1996 from nine pesos in 1995, he said.
Bulk agriculture shipped from Progreso, Yucatan rose to 8,500 tonnes per day from 1,000 tonnes in 1995.

Foreign participation in port administration is limited to a maximum 49 percent, while in labor management, general shipping services, navigation and construction, complete foreign control is allowed, the report said.
Maritime transport accounts for 32.8 percent of all cargo moved, of which 62.9 percent is petroleum products, 25.5 percent minerals, 4.5 percent agriculture and the remainder general cargo.
The three main crude shipping ports handled most of port cargo, with Coatzacoalcos handling 15.5 percent, Cayo Arcas controlling 15.2 percent, followed by Dos Bocas with 11.1 percent.
Coatzacoalcos handled 31.61 miillion tonnes of cargo in 1996, followed by Lazaro Cardenas with 12.02 million tonnes, Tampico/Altamira with 10.72 million tonnes and Veracruz with 9.86 million tonnes.
For container ports, Veracruz shipped 265,171 twenty-foot equivalent units (TEUs), followed by Tampico/Altamira with 181,211 TEUs and Manzanillo with 172,004 TEUs, the report said.
